title: Model pin resolution policy and SDK mapping for tags, semver, and commit hashes
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Customers need deterministic, auditable ways to pin model selection in the Redwood API and SDKs. Current behavior is underspecified for overlapping selectors (tags, semver ranges, and commit hashes) and for environments (hosted, dedicated, private) which can cause surprising rollouts or silent quality regressions. This ticket defines a concrete resolution policy, SDK surface changes, telemetry hooks, and a staged migration path for client libraries and runtime.

Proposal: 1) Canonical selector types: a selector in requests can be one of: 'tag:<name>', 'semver:<range>', 'ref:<commit-hash>' or an explicit model-id (immutable backend identifier). 2) Precedence rules: if multiple selectors are present, resolver uses precedence: ref (highest) > model-id > semver range > tag (lowest). If a selector resolves to multiple candidates (e.g., semver range returns multiple compatible builds), pick the highest-stability candidate as defined in the published performance profile (stability score). 3) Fallbacks: allow optional fallback chain parameter in SDK/API: e.g., primary=semver:^1.2.0, fallback=tag:latest-stable. 4) Compatibility tiering: tags can be annotated with compatibility meta (major/minor compatibility). When an exact semver match exists prefer exact; otherwise prefer semver-compatible candidates annotated as compatible for the runtime's target architecture/quantization profile. 5) Auditing and warnings: server returns a resolution header (X-Redwood-Model-Resolved: <model-id>) and a deprecation/warning header when selector semantics will change or when selector resolves to a preview build. SDKs must surface a non-fatal warning log and optional exception hook when client-configured strict mode is enabled. 6) Private and Dedicated deployment considerations: hosts may override public tag-to-model mappings; resolver must consult local registry if provided and fall back to central registry only if 'allow_central_fallback' is true.

Rationale and trade-offs: - Prioritizing ref/commit gives deterministic reproducibility for debugging and SRE playbooks. - Lowering tag precedence avoids accidental drift from floating tags (e.g., 'latest'). - Allowing explicit fallback chains keeps client ergonomics for PLG users while giving enterprises the ability to lock to exact refs. - Adding telemetry on resolution decisions enables us to detect silent rollouts and quality regressions.

API surface changes: - New request field: 'selector' (string) and optional 'fallback_selectors' (list of strings). - New response headers: 'X-Redwood-Model-Resolved', 'X-Redwood-Model-Resolution-Chain' (comma-separated selectors), and 'X-Redwood-Model-Profile-Id'. - New error codes: MODEL_RESOLUTION_CONFLICT, MODEL_RESOLUTION_NOT_FOUND.

SDK changes: - Add helpers for constructing selectors: Selector.byTag("stable"), Selector.bySemver("^1.2.0"), Selector.byRef("3b7a9f"). - Expose resolution metadata on the response object: resolvedModelId (string), resolutionChain (list of strings), profileId (string). - Add client option 'strictModelResolution' (boolean) to fail fast if resolved model differs from client expectation. - Emit structured telemetry event 'model_resolution' with fields: requested_selectors, resolved_model, resolution_path, environment, tenant_id.

Acceptance criteria and testing: see list below.

Rollout plan: 1) Implement server resolver and headers behind feature flag. 2) Add server tests and integration tests with private registry overrides. 3) Release SDK changes in minor versions with opt-in 'strictModelResolution' defaulting to false. 4) Run a canary for hosted API with telemetry to validate no large-scale unexpected resolution changes. 5) Announce migration docs and sample migration scripts.

Docs and artifacts: link to PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Model+Pinning+Resolution+Policy (placeholder), RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/492, initial server implementation branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/compare/feature/model-resolution (placeholder).
acceptance_criteria: Server accepts new selector syntax and returns resolution headers when feature flag enabled
Resolver implements precedence: ref > model-id > semver > tag
SDKs expose selector helpers and resolution metadata without breaking existing call sites
Fallback chains work end-to-end and are auditable via resolution headers and telemetry
Private/Dedicated registry override honored when configured
Automated integration tests cover semver ranges, tag drift, and commit pinning
tasks: Design and formalize selector grammar and publish in API spec
Add response headers and error codes in API gateway layer
Implement SDK bindings (JS, Python, Go) to expose helpers and resolution metadata
Add telemetry event and dashboard to track resolution churn
Write migration guide and sample scripts for customers
Coordinate with Dedicated/Private infra to support registry overrides
comments: 2025-02-13 | Liam O'Connor: Added initial precedence proposal. Need to confirm whether model-id should be considered higher than ref; I think ref must be highest for reproducibility.
2025-02-14 | Priya Shah (PM): Confirm support for fallback chains — customers use pinned semver but want last-known-good tag as fallback. We'll include opt-in fallback_selectors in request payload.
2025-02-15 | Marco Liu (Runtime): Runtime can resolve semver by consulting published manifest that includes stability_score and quantization profiles. We'll add a TTL to manifests to bound staleness.

2025-02-18 | Ella Nguyen (SDK): We should avoid changing existing response shapes. Plan to add fields under a new 'resolution' namespace on the response object and gate user-facing strict behavior behind a client option.
2025-02-19 | Security: Reviewed private registry override surface; flagged that registry auth tokens MUST be stored in customer KMS and never proxied through the central control plane.
2025-02-20 | Ava Martinez: Preparing branch and integration test matrix. Marking estimate at 5 points. Will follow up with telemetry dashboard mockups.
